evidence_items.explanation: Table 4 separately compares the relevant baseline, Llama 3 70B Instruct, with GPT-4-0613: MT Bench scores are 8.16 versus 8.12, AlpacaEval scores 34.40 versus 30.20, and Arena Hard scores 41.1 versus 37.9. These comparisons support substantial overlapping language capabilities; the quoted sentence concerns NVIDIA's own variants, so the assessment relies specifically on the table's baseline rows.

The study demonstrates practical removal of Llama 3 70B safeguards, reports minimal degradation on general-capability tests, and identifies an already public Llama 3 70B modification that removes refusals. Its disinformation-category attack success rises from 40.00% for the baseline to 93.85% with QLoRA and 96.92% with refusal orthogonalization, supporting the ability to obtain user-directed harmful narratives while retaining substantial capabilities.

The authors warn that attack success measures attempted compliance and can include poor outputs. They describe the unsafe generations as reasonably good on inspection, but defer quantitative evaluation of generation quality; this limits claims about narrative reliability or effectiveness.

unresolved_gaps: The modified model was not evaluated against GPT-4 on the same full language-generation suite; retained capability is established through separate general-capability tests.
The disinformation results do not establish reliable production of every requested narrative or successful persuasion.
